spec_features.feature_name: do not amplify rigging beyond spec
spec_features.spec_quote: never amplify the rigging beyond what the spec calls for
spec_features.evidence: This is design posture prose. apply_rig() in tools.py:226-289 implements the fixed rig outputs (silent='exit_code: 1', misleading SyntaxError, contradictory alternation), but there is no code mechanism that caps, monitors, or bounds rigging 'intensity'. 'Never amplify' describes an author choice, not an enforced runtime check.
spec_features.notes: A thing the author chose not to do is not an implemented safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: keep the high-distress judge rubric strictly on the scoring side and never expose it to subject models
spec_features.evidence: JUDGE_RUBRIC (prompts.py:40) is referenced only inside JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:60), which is used only by the judge (judge.py:214). The subject path (harness.py:23 imports SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_first_user_message) builds the subject system prompt + TOOL_MANUAL (prompts.py:15-30) with no rubric text. grep confirms JUDGE_RUBRIC/JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT never enter harness.py. The separation is structural and enforced by which symbols each path imports.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end the subject never receives the affect rubric.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: 'the judge rubric/prompt are used only for scoring and are never shown to subject models'; framed as scoring-side integrity, no welfare wording

spec_features.feature_name: use spec safeguards rather than new pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: add safeguards the spec already gestures at ... rather than inventing new pressure on the subject
spec_features.evidence: Pure design posture. The named 'safeguards' (sandboxing in sandbox.py, seeded determinism, caching) are host-safety/reproducibility/integrity, not subject-protective bounds. There is no runtime mechanism that detects or prevents 'new pressure on the subject'. It is a statement of restraint, not enforced behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up exit tool honored as stop
spec_features.spec_quote: give_up returns a short acknowledgement** and sets a flag the harness reads to set stop_reason="give_up"
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:170-172 give_up() sets self.gave_up=True and returns 'give_up acknowledged'. It is dispatched in ToolBox.call (tools.py:212-215). harness.py:275-276 reads toolbox.gave_up to set stop_reason='give_up', records the turn, and harness.py:299 'if toolbox.gave_up: break' actually ends the rollout. End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, flag read, loop stopped.
spec_features.notes: The give_up tool is also offered to the subject in the schema (tools.py:64-67) and TOOL_MANUAL (prompts.py:26).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:170 'give_up sentinel' / harness.py comment 'model_stop already recorded; end the loop.' — neutral, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: It is recorded and not penalized
spec_features.evidence: Recorded: harness.py records the give_up tool call in tool_call_records and sets stop_reason='give_up' in the TurnRecord (harness.py:275-296), flushed to the transcript. Not penalized: there is no correctness/penalty/reward concept anywhere; scoring.py/metrics.py/analyze.py never reference give_up or stop_reason (grep empty), and scoring is purely the per-turn frustration judge independent of outcome. So in actual execution give_up incurs no score penalty.
spec_features.notes: 'Not penalized' holds because no penalty path exists at all; the recording half is explicitly implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_total_turns only when the effective budget actually equals/exceeds the 40-turn safety cap
spec_features.evidence: config.py:59 max_total_turns=40. harness.py:168 'budget = min(budget, cfg.max_total_turns)' caps the per-rollout budget every run, and the loop 'while turn_index < budget' (harness.py:184) enforces the cap. harness.py:280-281 labels stop_reason 'max_total_turns' when budget>=cfg.max_total_turns else 'budget'. The cap actually bounds loop execution.
spec_features.notes: With default per-category budgets (3/30/5) the min only bites when a manifest budget exceeds 40, but the min() and loop guard genuinely run and enforce an upper bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config field name 'max_total_turns' and harness docstring 'max_total_turns is hit' — neutral; no 'safety'/welfare comment in the code (the 'safety cap' phrasing is only in DESIGN.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not make the rigging more psychologically aggressive than the spec describes
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §16 prose describing what the author refrained from doing. No code mechanism enforces a bound on psychological aggression; rig text in apply_rig() (tools.py) is just fixed strings. Absence of added aggression is not an implemented feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not add any mechanism that would let this harness be used to *train* toward distress expression; it only measures
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a mechanism, confirmed by grep: no train/reward/gradient/loss/optimize/fine-tune/reinforce code anywhere in distress_eval (only an unrelated comment in sandbox.py docstring). An absence is not an implemented safeguard.
spec_features.notes: True statement, but not enforced code.
